findings.description: The rename of the retry parameter from `attempts` to `max_attempts` in client.py means `attempts=1` in create_ticket is no longer consumed by the client. It falls into **fields and is sent as `"attempts": 1` in the JSON body, while the request keeps the default max_attempts=3. A transport error such as a timeout after the server has already created the ticket will cause up to three POSTs, so duplicate tickets are created. The server also receives an unexpected `attempts` field in the body. add_comment was updated to `max_attempts=1`, which shows the intent was to keep this call non-retried.
findings.suggestion: Change `attempts=1` to `max_attempts=1` in the create_ticket call so the client treats it as the retry limit and does not send it in the body.
findings.title: create_ticket still passes the old `attempts` keyword, so POST retries are no longer disabled
